title: Choosing a suitable aquarium
steps: Research the adult size and social needs of the fish you want before buying a tank.
Choose a tank large enough for the planned stock, with room for filtration and swimming.
Place it on a level, purpose-built stand.
caution: Small tanks can be less stable; never choose fish solely by their size in the shop.

title: Safe tank location
steps: Keep the aquarium away from direct sunlight, radiators and cold draughts.
Provide a stable stand and safe access to electrical sockets.
Leave space to maintain the filter and reach the tank safely.
caution: Water is heavy; check floor and furniture load capacity.

title: Aquarium cycling before fish
steps: Set up the filter and run a fishless nitrogen cycle using an appropriate ammonia source.
Test ammonia, nitrite and nitrate with reliable kits and record the readings.
Add fish only when the system processes the intended ammonia load without detectable ammonia or nitrite.
caution: Cycling can take weeks; do not assume clear water is safe.

title: Understanding ammonia
steps: Use a freshwater test kit to check ammonia, especially in new or troubled tanks.
If detected, check fish behaviour, reduce feeding and carry out an appropriate partial water change.
Investigate filtration or stocking issues.
caution: Ammonia is toxic; urgent corrective action may be needed.

title: Understanding nitrite
steps: Test nitrite during cycling and after filter problems.
If nitrite is detectable in an occupied tank, take prompt corrective steps including suitable partial water changes.
Keep the biological filter running and investigate the cause.
caution: Nitrite can impair oxygen transport in fish.

title: Monitoring nitrate
steps: Test nitrate and compare with the needs of the fish and plants.
Use regular partial water changes and sensible feeding to prevent buildup.
Record trends rather than relying on one reading.
caution: Nitrate targets depend on species and local water conditions.

title: Testing pH properly
steps: Test aquarium pH and the pH of your source water.
Choose species suited to your normal water chemistry.
Avoid chasing a perfect number with rapid chemical changes.
caution: Stable, species-appropriate conditions are often safer than sudden adjustments.

title: Water hardness basics
steps: Check general hardness and carbonate hardness of your source water.
Research whether chosen fish need soft or hard water.
Keep a record when choosing stock or making changes.
caution: Different fish have different mineral requirements.

title: Conditioning tap water
steps: Measure replacement water and dose a suitable aquarium dechlorinator according to its label.
Match replacement water temperature closely to the tank.
Add water gently without disturbing fish or substrate.
caution: Chlorine and chloramine can harm fish and beneficial bacteria.

title: Routine partial water changes
steps: Test the water and decide an appropriate change volume for your aquarium.
Siphon out part of the water while removing accessible waste.
Refill slowly with temperature-matched, conditioned water.
caution: Avoid changing all water at once during routine care.

title: Gravel vacuuming
steps: Use a gravel siphon to lift debris from accessible substrate.
Work in sections so fish and plants are not disturbed excessively.
Replace removed water with conditioned water.
caution: Avoid deep disturbance of substrates designed to remain layered.

title: Cleaning aquarium glass
steps: Use a dedicated aquarium algae pad or scraper appropriate to glass or acrylic.
Clean gently near seals and corners.
Remove loose debris during the next water change.
caution: Never use household detergents or abrasive tools on acrylic.

title: Maintaining a sponge filter
steps: Switch off the air pump safely before maintenance.
Gently squeeze the sponge in a bucket of removed aquarium water.
Reassemble and confirm airflow has resumed.
caution: Do not sterilise filter media or rinse it in untreated tap water.

title: Cleaning a canister filter
steps: Follow the manufacturer's shutdown and priming instructions.
Rinse mechanical media gently in removed tank water.
Keep biological media wet and restart promptly, checking for leaks.
caution: Do not replace all biological media at once.

title: Protecting beneficial bacteria
steps: Keep the filter running continuously except for short maintenance.
Avoid overcleaning all media at the same time.
Check water parameters after major equipment changes.
caution: A disrupted biofilter can cause dangerous ammonia or nitrite spikes.

title: Choosing filter flow
steps: Research whether your fish prefer gentle or strong current.
Position the outlet to circulate water without exhausting fish.
Use a spray bar or baffle if needed.
caution: Long-finned or small fish may struggle in excessive flow.

title: Air stones and surface movement
steps: Check whether your filter provides enough surface agitation.
Add an air stone if extra circulation is useful.
Observe fish for gasping or unusual behaviour.
caution: An air stone does not replace water-quality management.

title: Setting a stable heater
steps: Choose a heater sized for the aquarium and the species kept.
Use a separate thermometer to verify the temperature.
Check readings daily and protect the heater from damage.
caution: Unplug heaters before exposing them to air during water changes.

title: Using an aquarium thermometer
steps: Place a thermometer where you can read it easily.
Check for unusual changes morning or evening.
Compare with a second thermometer if readings seem wrong.
caution: Sudden temperature swings can stress fish.

title: Safe aquarium electrics
steps: Create drip loops below sockets and plugs.
Keep extension leads and adapters away from splashes.
Unplug equipment safely before wet maintenance.
caution: Water and mains electricity are hazardous; use an RCD-protected supply.

title: Choosing LED lighting
steps: Choose aquarium lighting suitable for your plants and fish.
Use a timer for a consistent day-night cycle.
Adjust duration if algae grows excessively.
caution: Avoid leaving bright lights on continuously.

title: Live plant selection
steps: Choose aquatic plants suited to your light and water conditions.
Check whether fish may dig or eat delicate plants.
Rinse and inspect plants before adding them.
caution: Avoid plants treated with chemicals unsuitable for aquariums.

title: Planting without damaging roots
steps: Remove packaging and damaged leaves.
Plant roots in suitable substrate without burying the crown of rosette plants.
Anchor or attach species that grow on wood and rock.
caution: Anubias and Java fern rhizomes should not be buried.

title: Trimming aquarium plants
steps: Use clean dedicated aquarium scissors.
Remove dead leaves and trim excessive growth gradually.
Siphon away cuttings and check filter intakes.
caution: Avoid major plant removal all at once in a heavily planted tank.

title: Managing algae safely
steps: Identify whether algae is linked to light, nutrients or maintenance.
Reduce excess lighting and remove algae manually.
Review feeding and water changes before considering treatments.
caution: Do not rely on algae-eating fish as a substitute for care.

title: Choosing compatible fish
steps: Research adult size, water chemistry, temperament and temperature needs.
Check whether species are schooling, territorial or predatory.
Plan stocking conservatively for the actual aquarium.
caution: Fish sold as small juveniles may grow very large.

title: Keeping schooling fish
steps: Research the minimum appropriate group size for each schooling species.
Provide open swimming space and cover.
Observe whether shy fish settle better in a suitable group.
caution: Do not buy extra fish if the tank cannot safely support them.

title: Introducing new fish
steps: Dim the lights and float the sealed transport bag briefly to reduce temperature differences.
Acclimate fish according to reputable species and retailer guidance, avoiding prolonged exposure to bag water.
Transfer fish with minimal transport water and observe quietly.
caution: Never pour shop water into the aquarium; acclimation needs vary.

title: Quarantining new arrivals
steps: Prepare a separate, cycled quarantine tank with suitable equipment.
Observe new fish for abnormal behaviour and signs of disease before adding them to the main tank.
Use separate nets and equipment where practical.
caution: Quarantine duration and treatment should be guided by an aquatic vet or experienced specialist.

title: Daily fish observation
steps: Watch swimming, breathing, appetite and social behaviour.
Check for torn fins, spots, swelling or unusual hiding.
Record changes and check water parameters promptly.
caution: Rapid breathing, loss of balance or multiple sick fish need urgent attention.

title: Responding to a sick fish
steps: Test ammonia, nitrite, temperature and other relevant parameters.
Record symptoms and check whether more than one fish is affected.
Seek qualified aquatic veterinary advice before using medication.
caution: Do not medicate blindly or combine treatments.

title: White spot awareness
steps: Watch for small white spots, rubbing and rapid breathing.
Check water quality and seek a reliable diagnosis.
Follow species-safe veterinary or specialist treatment advice.
caution: White spots can have different causes; some medications harm invertebrates.

title: Fin damage and fin rot
steps: Inspect fins for tears, fraying and redness.
Check for bullying, sharp decor and poor water conditions.
Get specialist help if damage progresses or infection is suspected.
caution: Avoid treating every torn fin with antibiotics.

title: Feeding the right diet
steps: Choose a quality diet suited to each fish species and feeding level.
Offer small portions they can consume promptly.
Remove uneaten food and monitor body condition.
caution: Overfeeding is a common cause of poor water quality.

title: Frozen fish foods
steps: Use commercially prepared frozen foods suited to your fish.
Thaw a small portion safely and feed with clean tools.
Discard leftovers rather than refreezing thawed food.
caution: Follow package handling instructions to avoid contamination.

title: Feeding bottom dwellers
steps: Choose sinking food appropriate to the species.
Feed when bottom-dwelling fish can reach it without competition.
Remove uneaten food and check all fish are eating.
caution: Catfish and loaches have different diets; they cannot live on scraps alone.

title: Avoiding overfeeding
steps: Measure portions instead of adding food by eye.
Watch for uneaten food and rising nitrate.
Adjust feeding to fish size, species and condition.
caution: Excess food breaks down and can harm water quality.

title: Planning holidays and fish feeding
steps: Arrange a trusted person to check the aquarium and feed pre-measured portions.
Leave clear instructions and an emergency contact.
Test any automatic feeder well before travelling.
caution: Avoid adding large amounts of food before leaving.

title: Caring for shrimp
steps: Check water chemistry and copper sensitivity for the shrimp species.
Provide hiding places and gentle filter intake protection.
Offer suitable food and observe moulting.
caution: Many fish prey on small shrimp; check compatibility.

title: Caring for aquarium snails
steps: Identify the snail species and its adult size.
Provide suitable food and minerals where needed.
Check that medications are safe for invertebrates.
caution: Never release unwanted aquarium animals into waterways.

title: Avoiding accidental pests
steps: Inspect new plants and decor for unwanted hitchhikers.
Quarantine or prepare plants using safe methods where appropriate.
Remove pests manually if needed.
caution: Never use household pesticides in an aquarium.

title: Safe decorations and wood
steps: Choose aquarium-safe rock, wood and ornaments.
Check for sharp edges, unstable stacks and trapped spaces.
Rinse new items without soap before placing them.
caution: Some rocks alter water hardness and pH.

title: Aquarium substrate choices
steps: Research whether your fish need sand, smooth gravel or specialised plant substrate.
Rinse substrates as directed before use.
Keep substrate depth and grain size appropriate for the species.
caution: Sharp gravel can damage sensitive bottom-dwelling fish.

title: Moving fish during a house move
steps: Prepare insulated fish-safe containers with tank water for short transport.
Keep filter media wet and preserve oxygen and temperature as practical.
Reassemble promptly and test water after the move.
caution: Long transport needs specialist planning; never seal fish in unventilated containers for extended periods.

title: Responding to a power cut
steps: Keep the aquarium insulated and avoid unnecessary opening.
If safe, provide battery-powered aeration.
Check temperature and water quality when power returns.
caution: Filter bacteria and oxygen levels can be affected by prolonged outages.

title: Responding to a filter failure
steps: Check power and safely inspect blocked intakes or impellers.
Provide aeration if possible while arranging repair.
Test ammonia and nitrite until filtration is stable.
caution: Never run a damaged electrical device in water.

title: Handling a heater malfunction
steps: Check temperature with a separate thermometer.
Disconnect faulty equipment safely and stabilise temperature gradually.
Seek an appropriate replacement promptly.
caution: Avoid rapid cooling or heating and never touch a broken submerged heater.

title: Avoiding cleaning chemicals
steps: Keep sprays, soap, polish and paint fumes away from open tanks.
Use dedicated aquarium buckets and tools.
Wash hands and rinse thoroughly before aquarium maintenance.
caution: Even small amounts of household chemicals can be toxic to aquatic life.

title: Preventing fish escapes
steps: Use a secure lid with appropriate gaps for cables and ventilation.
Check gaps near filter hoses and decorations.
Keep jump-prone fish in a suitably covered tank.
caution: Some fish can jump through surprisingly small openings.

title: Keeping a water-test log
steps: Record date, temperature, ammonia, nitrite, nitrate and pH.
Note water changes, new fish and equipment maintenance.
Look for trends and changes before problems become serious.
caution: A log helps identify causes but does not replace prompt action when fish are unwell.

title: Planning stocking changes
steps: Review current fish sizes and water quality before adding animals.
Research compatibility and quarantine plans.
Introduce new stock gradually and monitor the biological filter.
caution: Never add many fish at once to an immature aquarium.

title: Responsible fish rehoming
steps: Contact a reputable aquarium shop, rescue or experienced aquarist if you cannot keep a fish.
Share species, size and water requirements.
Transport animals in suitable fish-safe containers.
caution: Never release aquarium fish or plants into the wild.
